title: The growth-record studio
subtitle: Summer 1 • See ten days of evidence in forty minutes
objective: Set up a consistent growth record and use dated repeated measurements to describe change over time.

sow.exactOutcome: Set up and observe a plant-growth investigation over time (ICT to record).
sow.alignment: Develops the C34 setup and recording skills, then analyses supplied dated evidence within 40 minutes. An optional real class investigation continues over days; this single lesson does not claim to complete ten days of live observation.

priorLearning: A fair plan compares similar plants with one intended change.
Height and leaf condition provide complementary evidence.
success: Use a plant ID, date, unit and fixed height rule.
Read change across the supplied dates.
Retain variation and distinguish missing from zero.

vocabulary.meaning: A value that was not recorded; not the same as zero.

equipment: Printed shared evidence and one chosen pupil route; pencil; optional ruler; projector or offline HTML.
Optional established bean seedlings, labelled pots and trays; centimetre ruler; optional spreadsheet.
preparation: Print the shared evidence, one response route and exit page. Routes are alternatives, not a workload ladder.
Read the worked answers. Prepare an oral, pointing or adult-scribed route where useful.

The dated May 2027 table is constructed teaching evidence, not historical observations. All six plants start at 3 cm. Group A receives 5 mL daily and B 15 mL in the fictional plan; do not treat these as universal care instructions.

Optional setup: label a real plant, take one baseline reading and arrange future observation dates with an adult. Keep that record separate from the supplied data. The full ten-day analysis uses the provided table today.
safety: Use adult-selected non-toxic plants for any optional baseline; no tasting. Wash hands after handling plants or compost.
Keep small water volumes in trays away from devices and wipe spills. An adult checks ongoing plant care daily and records any necessary adjustment.
practicalAlternative: All core reasoning uses the supplied evidence and can be completed in 40 minutes without a live practical.

misconceptions.claim: The final height is the amount of growth.
misconceptions.correction: Growth in height is final minus starting height.
misconceptions.check: Compare 11 cm final with 3 cm baseline.

misconceptions.claim: No reading means zero growth or zero height.
misconceptions.correction: A missing reading cannot be replaced by zero.
misconceptions.check: Ask whether a measurement was actually made.

misconceptions.claim: Each repeat must have the same value.
misconceptions.correction: Individual plants vary; keep the observed differences.

access.supported: Short choices, word bank and pointing or adult-scribed reasons; same core scientific goal.
access.standard: Make a short evidence-based explanation or record using the supplied information.
access.stretch: Apply the core idea to a changed case, evaluate evidence or identify a limit.
access.regulation: Preview the sequence. Offer seated observation, quiet paired rehearsal, private feedback and a pass from public sharing. Routes respond to current access needs, not a diagnosis.

slides.title: A record should survive a change of observer
body: Use supplied evidence to see ten days.
slides.notes: State explicitly that animation steps through constructed records; no real plant grows ten days during this lesson.

slides.title: Retrieve the measurement rule
body: 1. Where does the height ruler start?
slides.notes: 1 soil surface. 2 cm. 3 track the same plant over time and preserve repeats.

slides.title: I set up the record before comparing
slides.notes: Think aloud: “I record B1, date, cm and 3 cm starting height. Later 11 cm does not mean 11 cm growth: 11 minus 3 is 8 cm.” Demonstrate one real baseline if ready, or use the labelled worked model.

visual.title: Use one height rule
visual.description: A ruler begins at the soil surface beside a seedling. The main shoot tip reaches 6 cm; measure from soil surface to shoot tip, without including pot height or forcing the plant straight.

elements.text: Measure the same part, from the same starting level.
Do not include the pot or straighten the shoot by force.

slides.title: I read time before height
body: Compare values at the same day.
The intervals are not all equal.
slides.notes: Shares I do time. Think aloud: “Day 3 to day 7 is four days, not three. The graph gives that interval more width. At day 10 the means are 6 and 11 cm.” Mean is an optional summary, explained as total divided by three; core pupils read individual rows.

visual.title: Read growth over time
visual.description: Axes start at zero. Horizontal spacing is proportional to elapsed days 0, 3, 7 and 10; height is in cm. Each plotted value is the exact mean of three supplied constructed readings; A is 3,4,5,6 and B is 3,5,8,11.

slides.title: I preserve a missing observation
body: Leave a gap and give the reason.
slides.notes: Shares I do time. Think aloud: “No one measured plant X, so I cannot write zero. I mark missing. Our supplied six-plant table happens to be complete.”

visual.title: A missing value is not zero
visual.description: Three example record states distinguish a valid measurement (6 cm), not measured (missing) and actual zero. A missing value must remain explicitly missing and should not be drawn as zero on a graph.

elements.text:
Leave a gap;
record the reason.

A number, not
a missing mark.

These are record examples, separate from
the complete growth table.

slides.title: The timeline evidence desk
body: Find B1 on day 0 and day 10.
slides.notes: W1: B1 goes from 3 to 11 cm; increase 8 cm. Have a pupil choose the date before the other reads the value. Step the model only after predicting.

table.caption: Constructed sample data; individual plants A1 and B1

slides.title: Keep the differences visible
body: B1, B2, B3 finish at 11, 12, 10 cm.
Should we change them to match?
slides.notes: W2: retain all three; natural variation is useful. At day 10 B plants are green with 5–6 leaves; A plants have 2–3 leaves and A3 slightly droops. Heights alone do not prove overall health or a universal best water amount.
slides.reveal: Describe the pattern and its limits; keep every reading.

slides.title: B1 starts at 3 cm and ends at 11 cm.
body: What is its recorded height increase?
slides.notes: Correct second option. Use a difference bar or counted steps if needed.

options.feedback: That is the final height, not the change.

options.text: 0 cm because one other plant was not measured
options.feedback: B1 has both measurements; a separate missing value does not erase them.

slides.title: Choose your science route
slides.notes: Set ONE route. All routes analyse the supplied dates within this lesson. Optional setup means one baseline today plus an explicitly future schedule. Standard graph values B1: (0,3), (3,5), (7,8), (10,11). Do not require mean calculation for core BUILD.

slides.title: Make your own evidence record
slides.notes: All routes analyse the supplied dates within this lesson. Optional setup means one baseline today plus an explicitly future schedule. Standard graph values B1: (0,3), (3,5), (7,8), (10,11). Do not require mean calculation for core BUILD.

slides.title: Check what the evidence can show
body: Point to the clue you used.
slides.notes: Shares independent time. Ask for a reason, not just a correct word. All routes analyse the supplied dates within this lesson. Optional setup means one baseline today plus an explicitly future schedule. Standard graph values B1: (0,3), (3,5), (7,8), (10,11). Do not require mean calculation for core BUILD.

slides.title: Lundy loop: improve the shared account
slides.notes: Listen to a selected pupil revision and visibly adopt a scientifically accurate contribution. Offer private, written or partner feedback.
slides.prompt: What made our growth statement more honest?
slides.reveal: Use change from baseline, keep repeats and leaf evidence, and show missing records as missing.

slides.title: Keep the useful change
slides.notes: Shares review time. Name how a pupil contribution changed a label, method or conclusion. Do not rank pupils.
slides.reveal: Use change from baseline, keep repeats and leaf evidence, and show missing records as missing.

slides.title: Three final checks
body: E2. A plant changes from 3 to 11 cm. What is its increase?
E3. Is a missing reading the same as zero?
slides.notes: Collect brief individual evidence. Use the answer key and re-teach the specified misconception if needed.

pupilPages.title: Shared evidence • Constructed growth records
pupilPages.intro: Same young bean species, matched starting height and conditions. A: 5 mL daily; B: 15 mL daily in this teaching example. Heights are cm; these are not universal care amounts.

blocks.text: Day 10 leaf notes: A has 2–3 leaves per plant; A3 slightly droops. B has 5–6 leaves per plant and green leaves. Means: A = 3, 4, 5, 6 cm; B = 3, 5, 8, 11 cm on days 0, 3, 7, 10.

blocks.prompt: W1. Find B1’s baseline and final height. What is the increase?
W2. Why keep B1, B2 and B3 as separate readings?

pupilPages.title: Route 1 • Read a plant record
pupilPages.intro: Use B1. Word bank: baseline / cm / 8 / missing.

blocks.prompt: S1. What is B1’s height on day 0?
S2. What is B1’s height on day 10?
S3. How much did B1 increase in height?
S4. Give one leaf observation that should accompany height.
S5. A reading not taken should be recorded as...

pupilPages.title: Route 2 • Create the growth display
pupilPages.intro: Use B1’s four readings. The horizontal positions already allow for unequal time intervals.

blocks.prompt: M1. State B1’s start, final height and height increase.

blocks.text: M2. Plot B1 on the axes; join successive recorded points. Keep the cm unit.

visual.title: Blank plotting axes
visual.description: Axes start at zero. Horizontal spacing is proportional to elapsed days 0, 3, 7 and 10; height is in cm. The pupil can plot B1 values from the shared table; no answer points are shown.

elements.text: Plot B1: supplied dates and heights

blocks.prompt: M3. Use the table and leaf notes to write one careful conclusion about these groups.
M4. Give one reason this cannot establish the best watering amount for every plant.

pupilPages.title: Route 3 • Audit the record and claim
pupilPages.intro: A report says: “All B plants grew exactly 11 cm, and 15 mL is best for every plant.”

blocks.prompt: T1. Use baselines and the three day-10 B readings to correct “grew exactly 11 cm”.
T2. Compare the day-10 ranges for A and B.
T3. Give two reasons the universal watering claim is too strong.
T4. Plan a valid response if a future observation is missed. What stays in the record?

pupilPages.title: Exit and reflection
pupilPages.intro: Point, draw, write or tell an adult.

blocks.prompt: E2. A plant changes from 3 to 11 cm. What is its increase?
E3. Is a missing reading the same as zero?
R1. Which idea did you improve or defend? What evidence helped?
R2. What useful question would you investigate next?

answers.label: Retrieval 1–3
answers.answer: 1 soil surface. 2 cm. 3 compare the same plant across dates and retain individual variation.

answers.label: We do W1–W2
answers.answer: W1 3 cm to 11 cm, increase 8 cm. W2 distinct individuals vary; keep 11,12,10 rather than manufacture equality. Add leaf notes and limit conclusion to these conditions.

answers.label: Hinge
answers.answer: Second option correct: 8 cm. 11 is final height; missing data in another record is not zero for B1.

answers.label: S1–S5
answers.answer: S1 3 cm. S2 11 cm. S3 8 cm. S4 e.g. B plants green with 5–6 leaves, A3 slightly drooping. S5 missing with a reason.

answers.label: M1–M4
answers.answer: M1 3 cm, 11 cm, increase 8 cm. M2 points (day,height) (0,3),(3,5),(7,8),(10,11), joined in order with units; time spacing is unequal. M3 in these constructed conditions B ended taller (10–12 cm versus A 5–7 cm) with more leaves, while repeats varied. M4 one species, pot size, stage, short interval and limited sample cannot cover all plants/conditions.

answers.label: T1–T4
answers.answer: T1 B final heights 11,12,10 cm from 3 cm baselines, so increases are 8,9,7 cm. T2 A 5–7 cm; B 10–12 cm; ranges do not overlap here. T3 any two: small sample, one species/stage/pot size, limited interval, specific growing conditions, height not full health. T4 mark missing and give date/reason; retain all actual observations; take a later reading with its real date rather than invent the missed one.

answers.label: Exit E1–E3
answers.answer: E1 starting measurement used for comparison. E2 8 cm. E3 no.

answers.label: R1–R2
answers.answer: Responses vary. Credit a scientific revision, evidence-based defence or relevant next question. A private or oral response has equal value.

teacherNotes: 40 minutes: opening 2, retrieval 3, I do 7, We do 8, hinge 3, independent 12, review 3, exit 2. Zero-minute slides share the named stage time.
BUILD uses the supplied Year 3 science anchor with age-respectful contexts for older pupils. Supported, standard and stretch are selectable routes within the pathway.

Interactive We do: predict first, test against the controlled SVG model or supplied evidence, then explain or revise. Shared W tasks offer the equivalent paper discussion. Animation is a teaching representation, not filmed experimental evidence.
Keep constructed evidence separate from actual class observations. Do not invent measurements or require internet research.
The exact group means are provided for the interactive summary; no rounding is required. Mean A: 3,4,5,6; mean B: 3,5,8,11 cm. Keep individual repeats available alongside the summary.
Secure core: consistent record identifiers and units, correct change from baseline, and an honest statement about missing or variable readings.

interactive.title: Step through the growth record
interactive.intro: Constructed dated data. Previous/next moves through observation dates, not real-time plant growth. Paper table gives every value.

growth.note: Constructed means of three plants in each group. May 2027 dates are teaching records. Fixed species, starting size and conditions; watering amounts are not universal care advice.

steps.question: At day 0 both group means are 3 cm. Is that a baseline or ten-day growth?

choices.feedback: Later change must be compared with this start.

visual.title: Use one height rule
visual.description: A ruler begins at the soil surface beside a seedling. The main shoot tip reaches 6 cm; measure from soil surface to shoot tip, without including pot height or forcing the plant straight.

elements.text: Measure the same part, from the same starting level.
Do not include the pot or straighten the shoot by force.

steps.explanation: A date, unit and consistent rule make later comparisons meaningful.

steps.question: B1 changes from 3 to 11 cm. What is its height increase?

choices.feedback: Subtract the 3 cm starting height from 11 cm.

visual.title: Read growth over time
visual.description: Axes start at zero. Horizontal spacing is proportional to elapsed days 0, 3, 7 and 10; height is in cm. Each plotted value is the exact mean of three supplied constructed readings; A is 3,4,5,6 and B is 3,5,8,11.

steps.explanation: The mean graph and individual B1 happen to share values here; the full repeat table still matters.

steps.question: A different plant’s reading is missing. Should it be plotted as zero?

choices.text: No; retain a gap and reason
choices.feedback: No reading is different from a measured zero.
